answer: Proof of Personhood via hardware-bound biometrics provides a ferrous lock on network access, preventing the growth of a virtual grove of illicit autonomous identities. By requiring agents to secure their signing keys within a secure enclave or vault, the system forces an attacker to acquire unique, physically verified biometric credentials for every new node. This imposes a significant capital cost that scales linearly with the number of Sybils, rendering mass account fabrication economically prohibitive.
